family: periodic block at the growing end, eaten by a disordered middle
summary: A periodic block (1^5 0 1^2 0)^k grows at the left end by one copy every three visits while a disordered middle of 1-runs eats it, now and then swallowing it almost whole; no halt in 10^11 steps; open.
title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1LC0LF_1RA1LD_1LB1LE_0LC0RD_---0RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_1LC0LF_1RA1LD_1LB1LE_0LC0RD_---0RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The left end is a periodic block that grows steadily; the middle of the tape is disordered and now and then swallows the block. No rule for the middle is known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 63,728 cells have been visited and 51,851 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.539). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: For every length n of the run and any tape around it: L (111110110)^n D> 1 R reaches L D> 1 (101101101)^n R; L (011011111)^n E> 0 R reaches L E> 0 (110110110)^n R; L (110)^n D> 1 R reaches L D> 1 (101)^n R. These are the moves the head makes across the long uniform stretches of the tape.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps

claims.text: For every length n of the run and any tape around it: L (111110110)^n D> 1 R reaches L D> 1 (101101101)^n R; L (011011111)^n E> 0 R reaches L E> 0 (110110110)^n R; L (110)^n D> 1 R reaches L D> 1 (101)^n R. claims.title: The collapses of the block
claims.text: Up to 10<sup>9</sup> steps the periodic block at the left end grows by one copy every three visits and is swallowed thirteen times, with 11, 9, 84, 36, 135, 100, 36, 324, 36, 36, 260, 999 and 36 copies just before; the value 36 recurs five times.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts exactly when state F reads a 0, which would have to happen inside the disordered middle.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. At its growing end this machine lays down a neat repeating pattern, three cells per visit; behind it, a disordered middle keeps changing and every so often swallows almost the whole pattern at once.

sections.heading: A neat end and a disordered middle
html: Stop the simulator whenever the head reaches a new cell on the left. The tape starts with a long periodic block, the word a = 1^5 0 1^2 0 repeated (at some times instead (1^8 0)^k, another word of nine cells). Each visit adds three cells, one copy of a every three visits, and Lean proves how the head crosses the block in both directions, for every length.

Behind the block the tape is disordered: runs of 1s whose lengths are multiples of 3, separated by 0 and 110. This middle keeps changing and eats the block from the inside. Mostly the block wins and grows, but 14 times in the first 109 steps it was swallowed almost entirely, the last time at step 401,140,791, when at least 749 copies went at once. A halt (state F reading a 0) would have to come out of the middle; nothing about it is understood yet.

sections.heading: The collapses are not random
html: The block of copies of 1^5 0 1^2 0 at the left end grows by one copy every three visits of the head and then disappears at once. Just before each of its thirteen collapses in the first 109 steps it had 11, 9, 84, 36, 135, 100, 36, 324, 36, 36, 260, 999 and 36 copies. Five of them at exactly 36 copies: the collapses are triggered by something regular inside the middle region, a clock that has not been identified yet.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.539). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 63,728 cells (37,689 left of the start, 9,934 right), with a density of 1s of 0.814.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
